title: Rotational Warm-Pool Scheduling & Tactical Run Card — June 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a pragmatic operational plan for rotating and scheduling warm GPU pools across regions to maintain a 15-20% DR reserve while minimizing cold-start cost. Goal is to reduce cross-region blast radius during regional outages and provide a simple, repeatable run card for SRE/ops to execute an emergency rotation or a preemptive bump.

High-level constraints and assumptions:
- Target reserve: 15% of global concurrent capacity for standard models, 20% for high-priority enterprise tiers.
- Acceptable steady-state target utilization: 60-75% for active serving nodes, not including warm pools.
- Warm pools should be in a partially pre-warmed state: model weights loaded to CPU memory and 2x worker processes primed per GPU (fast pre-warm).
- Supported GPU families: H100 (high-performance), A100 (balanced), L40s (cost-optimized).
- Regions in rotation: us-west1, us-east1, europe-west1, asia-southeast1.
- Cost cap for warm pools: 8% of monthly infra spend per region, adjustable by PM approval.

Current fleet snapshot (approximate as of 2026-06-01):
- Global total GPUs: 1,920 (H100: 640, A100: 960, L40s: 320)
- Regional splits: us-west1: 680, us-east1: 560, europe-west1: 420, asia-southeast1: 260
- Baseline steady-state concurrent tokens/sec: 14k tps (avg) with 72% fleet weighted utilization
- Configured warm capacity: 140 GPUs (7.3% of fleet) across regions (imbalance noted — too concentrated in us-west1)

Observed problem statements (why rotate):
1) Warm pools concentrated in us-west1 => single-region outage causes uneven failover pressure and >24h warm-up for some model variants.
2) Static warm pools are costly during predictable low-demand windows (weekends) but necessary for short spikes.
3) No formal schedule for rotating physical reserved capacity between regions leads to drift and stale pre-warms.

Proposed rotational scheduling plan (tactical):
- Concept: maintain a rolling 4-week rotation where each region holds the full warm-pool profile for 7 days then hands off to the next region. This yields predictable coverage and spreads thermal/capacity stress across all regions.
- Warm-pool profile per region (week active): target 10% of that region's steady-state serving footprint or minimum 8 GPUs, whichever is higher.
- Hand-off window: midnight UTC Sunday, coordinated with traffic low window and a 30m maintenance flag in console.
- Pre-warm procedure: 2h before hand-off, spin up containers on target region with model weights cached, validate KV cache load (smoke), then switch traffic fallback targets via routing policy for the warmed pool.
- Warm-pool composition: mix of H100 and A100 matching model distribution for region; L40s excluded from primary warm pool (used for low-priority batch only).

Failover mapping (simple lookup table for ops):
- Tier-1 (enterprise low-latency): primary region -> fallback region -> reserved warm pool region (example: us-west1 -> us-east1 -> europe-west1)
- Tier-2 (standard): circular fallback order following rotation calendar (next region in rotation)
- Tier-3 (best-effort): route to cheapest available quantized model in same region, then cross-region if latency SLOs violated

Tactical run-card: emergency warm-pool bump (incident steps)
1) Detect: Pager triggers on region outage (monitoring alert: regional AZ outage or >30% packet loss to control plane).
2) Initial assessment (5m): SRE on-call confirms affected region and determines which model tiers are impacted using per-route dashboards.
3) Immediate actions (5-15m):
   - Trigger autoscaling policy 'rotate-bump' with +30% warm-pool instance target in next healthy region (console toggle or infra API call).
   - Update smart routing to prioritize fallback region for Tier-1 flows (automated failover flag).
4) Pre-warm accelerate (15-45m):
   - Use 'fast-prewarm' job to load model checkpoint into GPU memory on reserved nodes; run smoke sequences for top 10 prompts.
   - Validate latency 99th pctl < SLO for Tier-1; if failures, increase warm count or activate emergency canary in second fallback region.
5) Traffic migration (45-90m):
   - Gradually shift traffic using traffic-slicing policy: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3x 10m steps with tracing enabled.
6) Confirmation & stabilization (90-180m):
   - Confirm token costs, queue lengths, and per-token latency. Open a post-mortem ticket and tag incident owner.

Simulation snapshots and recommended safety margins (modelled with synthetic x1.8 spike):
- Baseline reserve 15%: reserve exhausted in ~7.5h when warm pool concentrated in single region.
- Rotational reserve (as proposed): reserve sustains ~22h under same spike due to distribution and faster pre-warm hand-offs.
- Recommendation: raise global target reserve to 18% and maintain regional minimum of 8 GPUs until Q3 demand trends are clearer.

Operational automation and monitoring checklist:
- Add 'rotation-week' label to infra resources and expose in console UI for visibility.
- Alerting: create alerts for warm-pool drift (>10% deviation from scheduled target), pre-warm fail rate >5%, and cross-region failover latency >200ms.
- Dashboards: per-region warm-pool utilization, cost-per-hour, pre-warm success rates, and warm-to-serve conversion time.
- Runbook CLI: small script to execute warm-pool handoff steps (sequence ID, region from, region to, smoke prompts list) — tracked in GitHub PR referenced above.

Cost impact and mitigations:
- Estimated monthly incremental cost to expand rotation to 18% reserve: +6.8% infra spend (~$120k/mo).
- Mitigation levers: shorter pre-warm retention during nights, use of spot-backed warm nodes for non-critical pools, quantized fallback model families for Tier-3.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Implement rotation-week label and console flag (owner: Luis Romero) — due 2026-06-18
- Create pre-warm smoke prompt set and attach to runbook (owner: Maya Kapoor) — due 2026-06-10
- Automate hand-off CLI and add safety checks (owner: Ethan Brooks) — due 2026-06-24
- Update escalation playbook and rerun simulation with real traffic trace (owner: Sofia Patel) — due 2026-06-30

Open questions & tradeoffs (notes):
- How much of warm-pool should be H100 vs A100 by region? Cost vs latency tradeoff will vary by customer mix.
- Should we commit to 18% global reserve as policy or keep it as a sliding target tied to 7-day rolling 95th pct demand?
- Legal/compliance: confirm whether cross-border warm pools for EU enterprise customers require different handling (consult security/compliance).

Notes to self / shorthand (informal):
- Slack channel for run-exec: #infra-warm-ops
- Jira epic for automation: INF-4200 (automation + dashboarding)
- Link to billing runbook for temporary budget increases 

End of doc — this is intentionally operational and lightweight. Will convert to a more formal playbook once run through two scheduled rotations.
